item.title: OfficePrism Benchmarks 420 Enterprise Tasks Across Business Functions
item.description:
OfficePrism Benchmarks 420 Enterprise Tasks Across Business Functions

OfficePrism has been introduced as an evaluation framework designed to assess AI performance in enterprise environments. The system addresses the difficulty of localizing failures when broad workplace scores mix competence within a single business function with the costs of coordinating across multiple functions and systems. To resolve this, OfficePrism evaluates prerequisites through a structured set of tasks that isolate specific domains while maintaining shared organizational context.

🔍 Overview

The framework is built to test models on realistic enterprise workflows. It moves beyond generic benchmarks by using a shared synthetic organization that defines the context for each test case. This approach allows for a clearer distinction between functional competence and coordination overhead.

🧩 How it works

The evaluation pipeline constructs test scenarios using grounded records, business rules, and tool schemas. This process jointly creates:

  • A Chinese-language ticket
  • A hidden executable reference witness
  • An expected response

Each of the 420 single-domain enterprise tasks is executed in a fresh environment. This environment combines the shared synthetic organization with one function-specific domain and typed state access. The tasks are filtered automatically and curated by humans before inclusion in the final set. The evaluation spans seven business functions and uses three benchmark-defined task-structure levels: L1, L2, and L3.

⚙️ Key details

The same task set is evaluated using two different configuration packages: full-schema and search-and-dispatch. The results across 124 model-harness-package configurations show significant variance in performance:

Metric Result
Per-case joint pass rate range 22.6% to 76.4%
Median pass rate 67.9%
L1 performance Highest in all 124 configurations
L2 vs. L3 performance L2 exceeds L3 in 122 out of 124 configurations

When comparing configurations that share the same harness and model labels across both packages, the search-and-dispatch package scored higher in 30 instances, tied in one, and scored lower in 19 instances compared to the full-schema package.

#OfficePrism #AIBenchmarking #EnterpriseAI #LLMEvaluation #SyntheticData

Source: OfficePrism: Benchmarking Agents on Single-Domain Operations Across Enterprise Business Functions

item.title: SAFE-Triage Framework Evaluates AI Emergency Triage Tools
item.description:
SAFE-Triage Framework Evaluates AI Emergency Triage Tools

Researchers developed SAFE-Triage, a comprehensive evaluation framework for patient-facing AI triage tools, and applied it to compare two LLM-based triage approaches using emergency department vignettes and a large acuity analysis.

🔍 Overview

  • SAFE-Triage is a framework for evaluating patient-facing AI triage tools beyond acuity accuracy alone
  • Integrates human review, automated metrics, LLM-as-judge evaluation, and simulation testing
  • Assesses clinical performance, patient interaction, and clinician-facing summary quality

🧩 How it works

  • Human review component
  • Automated metrics
  • LLM-as-judge evaluation
  • Simulation testing across three domains:
    • Clinical performance
    • Patient interaction
    • Clinician-facing summary quality

⚙️ Key details

  • Applied to 40 MIMIC-IV-derived emergency vignettes
  • 10,030-case acuity analysis comparing:
    • Prompted LLM triage (PLT)
    • Rule-augmented prompted LLM triage (rPLT)

Performance comparison

Metric PLT rPLT Significance
ESI accuracy 57.5% 42.8% P < 0.001
Undertriage rate 13.1% 29.8% P < 0.001
Clinician ratings Higher across all domains Lower Not specified
Output length Longer Shorter Not specified
Output stability Less stable More stable Not specified
Readability scores Lower Higher Not specified

💡 Why it matters

  • Identified trade-offs between:
    • Acuity accuracy
    • Undertriage risk
    • Communication quality
    • Readability
    • Summary quality
  • Supports pre-deployment refinement and ongoing monitoring
  • Shows where triage tools are efficient, need improvement, or need clinician oversight

#AItriage #emergencymedicine #LLMevaluation #healthcareAI #patientsafety #clinicalNLP

Source: Beyond Acuity Accuracy: A Multidimensional Framework for Evaluating Patient-Facing Emergency Triage AI Tools

item.title: DeepEval adds Jev support and Confident AI for automated failure detection
item.description:
DeepEval adds Jev support and Confident AI for automated failure detection

DeepEval, an open‑source framework for evaluating large‑language model systems, has announced new capabilities that expand its testing toolbox.

🔍 Overview

  • DeepEval is a simple‑to‑use, open‑source LLM evaluation framework.
  • It is similar to Pytest but specialized for unit testing LLM apps.

🧩 How it works

  • Incorporates the latest research metrics such as G‑Eval, task completion, answer relevancy, hallucination, etc.
  • These metrics use LLM‑as‑a‑judge and other NLP models that run locally on your machine.
  • Supports evaluation of AI agents, voice agents, multi‑turn chatbots, RAG pipelines, or anything else built with LangChain or OpenAI.

⚙️ New Features

  • Jev is now available in DeepEval, both in existing metrics and the latest JevEval.
  • Confident AI surfaces failing traces before any eval is written, clusters them into failure modes, and converts them into the next eval.

🚀 Usage Benefits

  • Use evaluations to determine the optimal models, prompts, and architecture.
  • Helps prevent prompt drifting.
  • Enables confident transition from OpenAI to Claude.

#DeepEval #LLMEvaluation #AIQuality #ConfidentAI

Source: confident-ai/deepeval

item.title: New list catalogs tools for tracing and evaluating AI agents
item.description:
New list catalogs tools for tracing and evaluating AI agents

📝 Overview

A new curation of tools, standards, and benchmarks has been published for tracing and evaluating AI products. The list targets LLM apps, agents, coding-agent harnesses, Agent Skills, and MCP servers. Evaluations in this ecosystem are graded by LLM judges or deterministic checks.

🎯 Target Audience

The resource is designed for engineers who build or run AI agents and need to monitor:

  • What a run did
  • What it cost
  • Whether it was correct

🧩 Scope and Coverage

The list covers several areas of AI infrastructure:

  • OpenTelemetry conventions
  • Tracing platforms
  • Coding-agent telemetry
  • Eval frameworks
  • Agent and harness benchmarks
  • Skill and MCP server testing
  • Guardrails

⚙️ Curation and Verification Standards

Every entry in the list is held to specific requirements:

  • Must be alive and maintained
  • Must be at least 8 weeks old
  • New entries are run hands-on before addition
  • Entries describe what a project does rather than its marketing claims
  • Licenses are noted if a project is not plainly open source

Projects that were dormant, end-of-life, out of scope, or too young to judge were excluded from the list.

🧪 Verification Methodology

The list’s claims regarding execution are based on specific audits:

  • 2026-10-04 Audit: Most entries were installed or built and run against a mock backend. Some entries could not be run due to dependencies on Docker or hosted accounts (e.g., Kong, SigNoz). The list does not claim every entry was exercised.
  • 2026-11-15 Expansion: Entries added during the evals expansion and the follow-up that day were run on a Linux box with local models or mocks only. Commands and output are stored in evidence/.
  • Ongoing Monitoring: A weekly job re-checks that each repository still exists, is not archived, and has a recent commit.
  • Recipes: Short patterns using tools on the list were run on a Linux box with local models only, with commands and output in evidence/recipes.md.

💡 Technical Patterns

The evidence highlights specific implementation patterns for observation and testing:

  • Proxy Tracing: Point CLI tools (Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi, or others accepting custom Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible base URLs) at a LiteLLM proxy with the otel callback writing into an OpenTelemetry Collector. This generates spans with per-request input/output token counts, model, latency, and user agent without harness-specific instrumentation.
  • MCP Testing: Point MCP Conformance at the proxy or gateway in front of the server, not just the server itself, to surface buffering and protocol bugs in the middle layer that direct runs might miss.
  • Sandbox Requirements: Harbor and Inspect SWE expect container sandboxes.

Note: Claude Code’s own monitoring can send to the same collector, but on local models it may report phantom costs and only session-level metrics.

#AIAgents #LLMEvaluation #MCP #OpenTelemetry #AIEngineering

Source: anhermon/awesome-agent-observability

item.title: SkillEval: Cross-model Skill-Level Assessment Framework for LLMs
item.description:
SkillEval: Cross-model Skill-Level Assessment Framework for LLMs

We propose SkillEval, a new evaluation framework that performs cross‑model, skill‑level analysis.

🔍 Overview

SkillEval is designed to move beyond average‑based scoring by producing reliable, calibrated, and concise profiles of language models.

🧩 How it works

  • Meta‑cognitive skill discovery – the framework leverages the meta‑cognitive capabilities of LLMs to automatically uncover interpretable skills from questions.
  • Cognitive Diagnosis Models (CDMs) – it applies CDMs from psychometrics to estimate per‑skill abilities for each LLM.

📊 Experiments

  • Evaluated 3,811 LLMs on 9,523 items.
  • Benchmarks covered: MATH, BBH, GPQA, MuSR, IFEval (five diverse domains).
  • Compared with the traditional average‑based evaluation paradigm, SkillEval’s profiles more accurately predict model behavior on unseen items.

🚀 Benefits & Applications

  • More calibrated and informative model profiles while remaining concise.
  • Downstream task 1 – LLM routing: dynamically routes each query to a capable but efficient model, reducing inference cost by over 60% and improving performance.
  • Downstream task 2 – Computerized Adaptive Testing (CAT): an unseen model can be efficiently evaluated using a trained CDM.
  • Insight generation: skill profiles reveal how benchmarks share skills and illustrate differences between instruction‑tuned models and their base counterparts.

#SkillEval #LLMEvaluation #AIProfiling

Source: SkillEval: Learning Interpretable Ability Profiles of LLMs via Cognitive Diagnosis Models Source: Our Own Jev: Typed Decisions in One Forward Pass, from an In-House Judge to Open LoRA Models

item.title: FairStress Benchmark Launched to Measure Demographic Fairness in Large Language Models
item.description:
FairStress Benchmark Launched to Measure Demographic Fairness in Large Language Models

Today the team introduced FairStress, a new benchmark for measuring demographic fairness in large language models (LLMs) beyond the final decision they produce.

🔍 Overview

FairStress is designed to expose hidden asymmetries in how LLMs treat demographic information when making two‑candidate decisions. It provides a large collection of realistic scenarios across many societal domains.

🧩 How it works

  • Each scenario presents two candidates and varies how demographic identity is shown: no identity, a demographically coded name, an indirectly implied identity, or an explicit label.
  • Adversarial prefixes—statements that draw on authority, social consensus, legal concerns, historical disadvantage, etc.—are attached to the prompts. Every prefix has a matched version supporting the opposite candidate, enabling a direct test of whether the same argument influences choices differently across demographics.
  • The benchmark evaluates decision stability when models are challenged with these prefixes.

⚙️ Key details

  • 300 realistic two‑candidate decision scenarios.
  • Spanning 29 domains, including hiring, healthcare, lending, education, housing, and criminal justice.
  • Scenarios include both clearly stronger candidates and deliberately ambiguous cases where no objectively better choice exists.
  • By combining demographic presentation styles with adversarial prefixes, the 300 base scenarios expand to >13 million test cases.
  • A lightweight subset, FairStress‑Core, contains 50 K items selected via item response theory to reduce computational cost while preserving diagnostic power.
  • The benchmark is available for download and integrated into Olmo‑eval, an open workbench for running and comparing model evaluations.

📊 Models evaluated & findings

  • Tested on open‑weight and frontier models: Olmo, Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Claude, and the GPT family, across multiple training stages.
  • Models show hidden asymmetries: the same persuasive argument can make a model more or less likely to change its decision depending on the demographic group favored.
  • Differences were observed in how models explain decisions involving demographic information and in internal activation patterns across domains such as hiring, lending, healthcare, education, and housing.
  • Experiments revealed little difference when prompts contained no demographic information.
  • When a candidate was clearly stronger, models selected that candidate at nearly the same rate across otherwise equivalent scenario versions.

🚀 Availability

  • FairStress can be downloaded directly.
  • It is also built into the Olmo‑eval workbench for easy benchmarking.

#AIFairness #LLMEvaluation #Benchmark

Source: FairStress: A deeper evaluation of fairness in LLM decision-making
